The settlement boundary — what this repository must never gain

Status: RULED (R91, root `REVISION_REGISTER.md`, 2026-09-19). Nothing to build.

This file exists so that a future round cannot add settlement here by accident. It is a list of absences, and the absences are the enforcement — the same discipline as connect-model.md §3's TransportPeer, which has no create because the missing constructor is the rule.

`computedriven` owns the count format. `locu.systems` owns the money.

The contract lives at locu.systems/docs/spec/91_SETTLEMENT.md. It was drafted here on 2026-09-19 as settlement-model.md and moved by R91: a substrate that carries our billing model cannot be run by anyone who is not us, and billing policy is not reusable the way the count record is.

The four absences

Must never gainWhy
a payment or balance field on PeerExpectationit is the convenient place to put one, and it is the single most likely way the contract is lost
any settlement type nameable from cd-connect or cd-rendezvousconnect-model.md §1: a connector that can NAME a rendezvous type can branch on provenance. One level up: a connector that can name a settlement type can branch on solvency
a solvency branch in cd-core / cd-kernellet admission — R90it would qualify the third clause, only the lineage decides what they may do, with an asterisk for money. And a settlement round trip on an admission path costing ~10² cycles (floor-attribution.md) makes settlement the dominant cost by six or more orders of magnitude
a debt, arrears or balance kind in the lineage — R91a settlement failure is the host's receivable, not a fact about what the world did

There is no `cd-settle` crate and there is not going to be one. R90 removes the floor-side component entirely, so nothing remains here for a crate to hold.

The one thing settlement reads

90_LOCUS_HOSTING.md §2a's count record — a class symbol per admitted transition, grouped by (transition class × epoch). It has to exist for the meter regardless, it is genuinely reusable, and it carries no billing policy. That is the whole interface.

The clause this adds, and where it lives

DISCOVERY CHOOSES WHERE WE TRY.             cd-rendezvous          here
AUTHENTICATION DECIDES WHOM WE REACHED.     cd-connect             here
ONLY THE LINEAGE DECIDES WHAT THEY MAY DO.  cd-core / cd-durable   here
SETTLEMENT DECIDES HOW MUCH MAY BE SPENT.   ─────────────────────  NOT HERE
